children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Tārā</s>, the swift and heroic one, whose eyes are like flashes of lightning,
who arose from the opening corolla of the face-lotus of the Lord of the Three Worlds (<s>Trailokyanātha</s>). || 1 ||
Homage to her whose face is like a hundred full autumn moons assembled,
O <s>Tārā</s>, blazing with the laughing rays of a thousand stars. || 2 ||
Homage to her adorned with hand-lotuses of golden blue water-lily hue,
whose domain is generosity, vigor, austerity, patience, forbearance, and meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>). || 3 ||
Homage to her who moves in endless victory at the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
attended by the sons of the Conqueror (<s>Jinaputras</s>) who have attained all the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections). || 4 ||
Homage to her who fills the directions and the ends of space with the syllables TUTTĀRĀ HŪṂ,
trampling the seven worlds with her stride, able to summon all without exception. || 5 ||
Homage to her worshipped by <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Maruts</s>, and <s>Viśveśvara</s>,
praised by hosts of <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits), <s>vetālas</s> (vampires), <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), and <s>yakṣas</s>. || 6 ||
Homage to her who with TRAṬ and PHAṬ destroys the devices of others' <s>mantras</s>,
with right leg drawn in and left extended, blazing with a whirl of <s>śikhī</s> (fire) flames. || 7 ||
Homage to <s>TURE</s>, the greatly terrifying one, destroyer of the heroes of <s>Māra</s>,
with wrathful frown on her lotus-face, slayer of all enemies. || 8 ||
Homage to her adorned at the heart with the <s>mudrā</s> of the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), fingers displayed,
adorned with the wheels of all the directions in their multitude, with light in every quarter. || 9 ||
Homage to her whose joyful tiara radiates garlands of light,
who with laughing, laughing TUTTĀRĀ subdues <s>Māra</s> and the worldly realms through terror. || 10 ||
Homage to her who can summon all the hosts of earth-guardians and the netherworlds,
who with frown and the syllable HŪṂ liberates from all misfortune. || 11 ||
Homage to her blazing with ornaments — a tiara bearing the crescent moon's segment,
ever radiant with rays of light, from <s>Amitābha</s> in her crest shining forth. || 12 ||
Homage to her who strikes the earth with her palms and tramples it with her feet,
who with frown and the syllable HŪṃ shatters the seven netherworlds. || 13 ||
Homage to her who abides amidst the garland of flames of the fire at the end of the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age),
who in the joy of the <s>ālīḍha</s> (warrior) posture destroys the circle of enemies. || 14 ||
Homage to her who is auspicious, virtuous, and peaceful, whose domain is the peace of <s>nirvāṇa</s>,
endowed with <s>SVĀHĀ</s> and <s>PRAṆAVA</s> (OṂ), destroyer of great sins. || 15 ||
Homage to her who in joy shatters the bodies of enemies,
illuminated by the <s>vidyā</s> HŪṂ, arrayed with the ten-syllable foot-mantra. || 16 ||
Homage to <s>TURE</s>, who stamps her feet, whose seed-form is the syllable HŪṂ,
who causes the trembling of <s>Meru</s>, <s>Maṇḍala</s>, <s>Kailāśa</s>, and the three worlds. || 17 ||
Homage to her who holds in her hand the deer-marked [moon] in the form of the lake of the gods,
who with twice-uttered PHAṬ accompanied by HARA destroys all poisons. || 18 ||
Homage to her attended by hosts of gods, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>kinnaras</s>,
whose armor of joy and splendor destroys nightmares and conflicts. || 19 ||
Homage to her whose eyes shine with the radiance of the full sun and moon,
O <s>Tārā</s>, who with twice-uttered TUTTĀRĀ dispels the most virulent fevers. || 20 ||
Homage to her who, endowed with the power of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, arranged in the three realities,
O supreme <s>TURE</s>, destroys hosts of <s>grahas</s> (seizing spirits), <s>vetālas</s>, and <s>yakṣas</s>. || 21 ||
This hymn, whose root is the <s>mantra</s>, comprises the twenty-one salutations.

children.text: yaḥ paṭhet prāyaśo dhīmān devyā bhaktisamanvitaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: Whoever, being wise, recites it regularly, endowed with devotion to the Goddess —

children.text: so 'yaṃ vā prātar utthāya smaret sarvābhayapradaṃ /
children.translated_text: that one, rising at dawn, remembering [her who is] the bestower of all fearlessness,
pacifier of all sins, destroyer of all miserable destinations —
is swiftly consecrated. Having attained greatness in this [life],

children.text: viṣaṃ tasya mahāghoraṃ smaraṇāt pralayaṃ yānti // 3
children.translated_text: the most terrible poison goes to destruction through mere remembrance. || 3 ||
For beings afflicted by fevers of <s>grahas</s> (planetary spirits) and poisons, and for others as well,
one desiring a son obtains a son; one obtains all desires. || 4 ||
Worshipped by seven <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors), at the end one goes to the state of <s>Buddha</s>hood.

children.text: sthāvaraṃ vātha jaṅgamaṃ sāḍ idaṃ pīḍam eva ca // 5
children.translated_text: Whether stationary or moving, even this very suffering — || 5 ||
the supreme destruction of affliction, for those who repeat [the hymn] two, three, or seven times,

children.text: dhanakāmo labhed dhanaṃ na vighnaiḥ pratihanyate // 6
children.translated_text: one desiring wealth obtains wealth and is not obstructed by hindrances. || 6 ||

body.text: iti śrīsaṃyaksaṃbuddhavairocanabhāṣitaṃ bhagavatyāryatāradevyā namaskāraikaviṃśatistotraṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ samāptaṃ // śubham //
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Namaskāra-ekaviṃśati-stotra</s> (Hymn of Twenty-One Salutations) to the Blessed Noble Goddess <s>Tārā</s>, spoken by the Perfectly Awakened One <s>Vairocana</s>, is completely finished. May there be auspiciousness!
